text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
MAARIV
- Wide searches for family that disappeared on way to wedding.
- Foreign Minister Levy: I will not run for prime minister.
- Justice Minister Hanegbi: Asks attorney general to see if police should investigate possible corruption in West Bank quarries.
- Officer that led group of Israeli officers touring death camps in Poland that gambled suspends himself.
- Police say their investigation succeeded in cutting off suspected 'Russian Mafia' figure from politicians.
- Navy acquires fast patrol boats from South Africa.

- Poll: If elections were held today 43 percent would vote for opposition Labour leader Barak, 35 percent for Prime Minister Netanyahu; 49 percent said Barak would better handle security matters, 29 percent said Netanyahu would; 46 percent believe Barak would be better negotiating peace, 31 percent believe Netanyahu would do better.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Committee will determine who will be nominated as army chief, head of Shin Bet secret service and of Mossad.
- Wide searches after five Israelis who disappeared in Jordan Valley of West Bank.
- Netanyahu wants to bring Palestinian security official to trial in Israel.
- In New York, son of a millionaire tortured to death for code of automatic bank teller card.
- Netanyahu commissioned poll to gauge popularity of Israeli President Ezer Weizman.
- Americans act on threat: Israel's El Al state airlines no longer can fly to Orlando, Washington and Texas.
JERUSALEM POST
- Levy slams Netanyahu disclosure of plan for final status arrangement with Palestinians.
- Missing family sought near Jericho.
- Labour party secretary general quits post.
- El Al banned on three U.S. routes.
- Central Bank considers capital inflow tax.
- Demand strong for Comfy IPO.
- Tadiran Telecom gets $10 million contract to supply Beijing Lian Tong Ren Economic Trade Company with wireless and wireline telecommunications systems.
GLOBES
- Deep disagreement between Benny Gaon and Stanley Gold on how to manage Koor.
HAARETZ
- Senior U.S. official says Israel and Palestinians should do all to make Egyptian mediation to solve peace crisis work because if U.S. re-engages it will not to be to either side's liking.
- Wide searches in Jordan Valley for missing family.
- Israeli police are for arresting some senior Palestinian Authority figures; Netanyahu is vacillating.
- Supervisors say they held foreign workers under brutal conditions; Labour ministry says all legal.
- Study shows 50 to 60 percent of drivers between cities break traffic laws.
